messages:
maria: FYI received a new pen-test finding (finding #7) — reporter claims KMS alias enumeration + a presign fallback chain that allowed generating presign tokens even when sessions were expired. They also tie it to a billing spike and higher tail latency for API calls. Attaching repro + CloudTrail snippets below. Need triage: scope, severity, evidence for customer. @jordan can you lead?

tyler: quick note from runtime side — presign endpoints should require full sigv4 + session validation. We did a canary change last night that touched auth fallback logic. I can pull the canary diff.

alex: SRE side: we see a spike at 2026-03-15T22:10Z in 5xx and retries, and a correlated jump in request count for /v1/presign. Trace IDs: trace-2034567890-1 and trace-2034567890-2. I'll attach raw traces to the ticket.

emily: CS: customer reported API errors and surprise billing. They want assurance keys weren't exfiltrated and a timeline of events. Requesting exact evidence package & retest plan.

jordan: we need a reproducible minimal PoC and CloudTrail evidence. Also want to confirm whether this impacts hosted only or Private/Dedicated too. @maria please post the repro steps (minimal curl) and the exact time window. We'll assemble mitigation and retest checklist.

maria: repro (attacker PoC) pasted below — minimal but shows behavior observed by pen tester:

```bash
# PoC - shows alias listing then presign fallback
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $POTENTIAL_TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Trace-Id: trace-2034567890" \\n  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/kms/aliases?limit=100'
# expected: 403 or empty for non-privileged, observed: 200 list with aliases

curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $POTENTIAL_TOKEN" \\n  -d '{"key":"alias/foo","expires":60}' \\n  'https://hosted.redwood.example/v1/presign'
# observed: 200 {"url": "https://...","token":"..."} even when session should be expired
```

maria: CloudTrail snippet (anonymized) pasted: 

```text
eventTime: 2026-03-15T22:10:12Z
eventName: GetPresignedUrl
userIdentity: assumed-role/redwood-frontend/ABCDEFG
requestParameters: { "key": "alias/foo" }
responseElements: { "presign": "true" }
```

tyler: digging: found a canary flag change. runtime-config `auth_fallback: true` was accidentally enabled in namespace `hosted-canary` between 2026-03-15T21:55:00Z and 2026-03-15T22:08:00Z. That would allow a fallback codepath to accept older session tokens. I have a PR to disable and will roll back canary.

alex: I've pulled logs and uploaded an evidence bundle to secure storage: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/2034567890/evidence.zip (access: security-only). It contains traces, CloudTrail extracts, and packet captures where available.

security-bot: Reminder: per process, upload to the secure evidence bucket and open SOC ticket. Created ticket SEC-6421 and attached evidence link.

emily: told the customer we're investigating and will run a retest after the rollback. Customer asked about SLA credits; been escalated to billing ops.

jordan: preliminary severity notes: initial pen-test scoring put this at P1 because it returns presign tokens, but exploitability requires possession of a bearer token. Given the fallback window and limited time window, propose marking as P2 once rollback is confirmed and evidence shows tokens cannot be minted. We will keep P1 until retest confirms.

maria: retest plan: 1) disable fallback in canary (tyler) 2) reproduce PoC (maria) 3) validate CloudTrail + HSM/CSP logs (alex/jordan) 4) deliver evidence bundle + timeline to customer (emily) 5) follow-up with billing if credits are requested. ETA 24 hours.

tyler: rolled back the canary at 2026-03-15T22:08:00Z — rollback entry id: deploy-7742. Observability now shows no auth_fallback path in traces.

maria: ran PoC against hosted endpoint at 2026-03-15T22:15:30Z and no longer returns presign token. Sample response: 

```http
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "insufficient_scope" }
```

maria: attaching retest notes and screenshots in the SOC ticket. Moving to "awaiting e2e verification". :white_check_mark: 

jordan: after we verify logs and HSM evidence we'll downgrade severity to P2 and close once CS confirms customer acceptance. Great work everyone.

emily: I'll draft the customer-facing timeline and next steps now.

alex: archived final artifact and set retention per policy. Closing loop on internal ops tasks.

maria: thanks all — will post final verification in SEC-6421 when done. :raised_hands:
